_meta.description: Every tax and benefit rule the engine uses. The engine reads rules only from here. See docs/m2-spec.md section 6 (tripwires).
_meta.verification: Each entry was checked against the official document named in its source on 2026-10-03 (see docs/rules-verification-2026-10.md). 'url' is the official link and 'lastVerified' the date it was confirmed. Where a page could not be fetched from the build session, 'verification' says so and 'lastVerified' stays null. Entries with lastVerified null are not to be used for new features; M1 keeps its own sourced copies in data/tax/2026.json.

rules.name: Standard deduction
rules.source: IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32, section 4.14
rules.verification: Confirmed against the revenue procedure on 2026-10-03. Section 2.08 notes the OBBBA made the higher standard deduction permanent.
rules.watch: Next year's values published each October

rules.name: Federal ordinary income brackets (taxable income; marginal; rates in percent)
rules.source: IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32, section 4.01, Tables 1 to 4
rules.verification: Every threshold typed from the four tables on 2026-10-03 and matched to data/tax/2026.json (identical).
rules.watch: Rates made permanent by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (2025); thresholds indexed yearly

rules.name: Top of the 0% long-term capital gains bracket (taxable income)
rules.source: IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32, section 4.03; IRC 1(h), 1(j)(5)
rules.verification: Single and joint confirmed; head of household and separate added from the same table.

rules.name: Long-term capital gains and qualified dividend brackets (taxable income; marginal; rates in percent)

value.stacking: Gains sit on top of ordinary taxable income: the 0% and 15% space is what is left of each threshold after ordinary income.

rules.source: IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32, section 4.03 (maximum zero rate and maximum 15% rate amounts)
rules.verification: Both thresholds for all four statuses typed from the table on 2026-10-03. The 20% rate above the 15% maximum is statutory (IRC 1(h)(1)(D)).

rules.name: Contribution limits
rules.source: IRS Notice 2025-67 (401(k), catch-ups, IRA); IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-19 section 2.01 (HSA); IRC 223(b)(3) (HSA catch-up, statutory $1,000)
rules.verification: All values confirmed on 2026-10-03. The Roth catch-up wage threshold ($150,000 of prior-year FICA wages) was added: catch-up contributions above it must be Roth from 2026.
rules.watch: Next year's limits published each fall. Roth catch-up requirement for higher earners begins 2026 (SECURE 2.0)

rules.name: Total annual additions limit (employee + employer + after-tax), IRC 415(c)

value.note: Catch-up contributions sit on top of this limit. Also capped at 100% of compensation.

rules.source: IRS Notice 2025-67; IRS COLA table

rules.name: Traditional IRA deduction phase-out (modified AGI)
rules.source: IRS Notice 2025-67

rules.name: Roth IRA contribution income phase-out (modified AGI)
rules.source: IRS Notice 2025-67
rules.watch: Above it, use the backdoor Roth

rules.name: Governmental 457(b) deferral limit (IRC 457(e)(15)), separate from the 401(k)/403(b) limit
rules.source: IRS Notice 2025-67 (457(e)(15) limit listed separately from the 402(g) limit); IRS COLA table
rules.verification: Amount confirmed. That the limit is separate follows from the two statutory limits being adjusted and listed separately; the IRS 457(b) topic page does not restate it.

rules.name: 72(t) substantially equal periodic payments

value.maxRate: greater of 5% or 120% of the federal mid-term rate for either of the two months before the first payment
value.duration: longer of 5 years or until age 59 and a half
value.modificationPenalty: 10% retroactively on all prior payments, plus interest
value.lifeTables: Uniform Lifetime, Single Life, or Joint and Last Survivor (Notice 2022-6 appendix)

rules.source: IRS Notice 2022-6, sections 3.01 and 3.02; IRC 72(t)(2)(A)(iv) and 72(t)(4)
rules.verification: Methods, 5% floor, 120% mid-term rate, and modification rules confirmed in the notice text on 2026-10-03.

rules.name: Rule of 55

value.appliesTo: the qualified plan (401(k), 403(b), pension) of the employer separated from, in or after the year of the birthday; not IRAs, SEP or SIMPLE IRAs, not earlier employers' plans

rules.source: IRC 72(t)(2)(A)(v) and 72(t)(10); IRS exceptions table
rules.verification: The IRS exceptions table confirms the separation-from-service exception applies to qualified plans only, at 55 (50 for public safety).

rules.name: Governmental 457(b) distributions are not subject to the 10% additional tax

value.exception: Distributions from a governmental 457(b) plan after separation are not subject to the 10% additional tax, except amounts attributable to rollovers from another type of plan or IRA

rules.source: IRC 72(t)(9); IRS exceptions table

rules.name: Roth IRA ordering and five-year rules

order: conversions and rollovers, first-in first-out (taxable part of each first, then nontaxable part)
value.conversionClock: Separate five-year period per conversion, starting January 1 of the conversion year; the 10% additional tax applies to the taxable part withdrawn inside it, only under 59 and a half
value.earningsClock: Five years from the first tax year a Roth IRA contribution was made, plus age 59 and a half (or death, disability, first home), for qualified (tax-free) earnings

rules.source: IRS Publication 590-B (2025), Roth IRAs: Ordering Rules for Distributions; Additional Tax on Early Distributions; What Are Qualified Distributions

rules.name: Federal poverty guidelines used for 2026 coverage (48 contiguous states and DC)

value.alaskaHawaii: higher; not entered (HHS page blocked from this session)
value.note: Premium tax credits for a coverage year use the guidelines in effect at open enrollment (the prior year's guidelines). Confirm which year's guidelines apply to 2026 credits before use.

rules.source: HHS poverty guidelines, as shown on HealthCare.gov
rules.verification: Values read from HealthCare.gov on 2026-10-03. The HHS/ASPE page (https://aspe.hhs.gov/topical-subjects/poverty-economic-mobility/poverty-guidelines) could not be fetched from this session: Eli to confirm there, including Alaska and Hawaii.

rules.name: ACA premium tax credit

value.tableMeaning: The percent of household income the household pays for the benchmark (second-lowest-cost silver) plan, interpolated linearly within each band. The credit is the benchmark premium minus that amount.

rules.source: IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-25, section 3 (applicable percentage table and required contribution percentage for 2026); IRC 36B
rules.verification: Table confirmed on 2026-10-03. The table stops at 400% of the poverty line, so the cliff is back for 2026 unless Congress acts.
rules.watch: Enhanced subsidies (no cliff, lower contributions) expired 2025-12-31. Bills to restore or extend them have been introduced. Check monthly.

rules.name: Medicare IRMAA tiers (monthly, 2026)

value.tierMeaning: A tier applies when MAGI from two years earlier is above its lower bound and at or below its upper bound.

rules.source: CMS fact sheet, 2026 Medicare Parts A and B Premiums and Deductibles (2025-11-14); SSA POMS HI 01101.020
rules.verification: Full Part B and Part D tables typed from the CMS fact sheet on 2026-10-03. The SSA POMS page could not be fetched from this session.

rules.name: Taxation of Social Security benefits (provisional income base amounts)
rules.source: IRC 86; IRS FAQ Social Security Income (base amounts); IRS Publication 915 (adjusted base amounts and 85% rule)
rules.verification: Base amounts confirmed on the IRS FAQ; the $34,000 and $44,000 adjusted base amounts and the 85% maximum confirmed in Publication 915 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p915.pdf).

rules.name: Senior deduction (age 65+)
rules.source: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Pub. L. 119-21) section 70103; IRS newsroom summary
rules.verification: Amount, thresholds, years, and stacking confirmed on the IRS page on 2026-10-03. The 6% phase-out rate is from the statute and is not restated on the IRS page: Eli to confirm (congress.gov could not be reached from this session).
rules.watch: Scheduled to end after 2028 unless extended

rules.name: Social Security trust fund outlook
rules.source: 2026 Social Security Trustees Report (released 2026-06-09)
rules.watch: Next Trustees Report; any legislation changing benefits or revenue

rules.name: Required minimum distribution start age

value.firstDeadline: April 1 of the year after reaching the start age; later years by December 31

rules.source: SECURE 2.0 Act section 107 (Pub. L. 117-328, Division T); IRS RMD topic page
rules.verification: Age 73 and the April 1 deadline confirmed on the IRS page on 2026-10-03. The 72 and 75 birth-year rules come from the statute, which is not restated on that page (congress.gov and govinfo.gov could not be reached from this session): Eli to confirm.

rules.name: Net investment income tax
rules.source: IRC 1411; IRS Tax Topic 559

rules.name: Social Security taxable maximum (wage base)
rules.source: SSA 2026 Cost-of-Living Adjustment fact sheet
rules.verification: Carried from data/tax/2026.json (retrieved 2026-10-02). ssa.gov blocks automated requests from this session, so it stays unverified here: Eli to open the fact sheet.

rules.name: HSA distributions: tax-free for qualified medical expenses (including saved receipts reimbursed later); otherwise ordinary income plus a 20% additional tax, with no additional tax from age 65
rules.source: IRS Publication 969 (2025), Distributions From an HSA: Additional tax and Exceptions; Recordkeeping
rules.verification: The 20% additional tax, its end at 65 (or disability or death), and the recordkeeping rule for later reimbursement confirmed in the publication on 2026-10-04.
